items.justification: Secure storage of security parameters versus due diligence on external components.
Examining telemetry for anomalies versus a threat modelling process that names data poisoning, model inversion and membership inference.
Secure storage of security parameters versus incident support for end users.
Validation of network input versus confidentiality of training and test data.
Disabling unused interfaces versus the patch delivery chain.
Encryption of security parameters in transit versus matching intended usage to data sensitivity.
Memory access control is an exploit mitigation; B concerns confidentiality of training data and weights.
Secure storage of security parameters versus communication of unresolvable threats.
Orderly network reconnection versus disaster recovery planning.
Both require guidance that lets the user operate the product safely, A on verifying secure setup, B on limitations and failure modes.
Examining telemetry for anomalies versus verifying that specified controls were built in.
Setup guidance for consumers versus an audit trail shared with downstream operators.
Cryptography for secure communication versus security testing before release.
Designed-in resilience and a support process during an incident are different obligations that together limit the impact of disruption.
Both concern security update notifications to the user; A gives the user control over them, B obliges the operator to send them.
Isolability of a non-updatable device versus maintaining an audit trail.
Disabling debug interfaces versus secure coding training.
Encryption of security parameters in transit versus due diligence on external components.
Authentication before network access versus security testing before release.
Both require a documented justification when the security baseline is departed from, A for unfulfilled provisions, B for poorly secured components.
Alerting on software tampering versus the risk of unused model capability.
Reviewed cryptographic implementations versus internal channels for threat updates.
Replaceability of cryptographic primitives versus maintaining an audit trail.
Verifying update authenticity versus secure deletion at decommissioning.
Informing the user of a required update versus the assessment preceding a decision to build.
Alerting on detected tampering versus advance notice of model updates.
Management of critical security parameters versus documentation of design and maintenance plans.
Both are documentation duties but of unrelated content and audience: sensing capabilities for users versus an internal audit trail.
Local operation during network loss versus assurance over an external risk owner.
Notifying the user of a required update versus disclosing how their data is used and stored.
Isolability of a non-updatable device versus documentation of training data sources.
Both require assurance before release, A that implementations have been reviewed or evaluated, B that the system was security tested.
Publishing a vulnerability disclosure policy versus maintaining an asset inventory.
Transparency about absent updates versus designed-in human oversight capability.
Both instrument the running system to surface security problems, A through telemetry, B through internal model state.
Recognizable model designation versus log analysis for model anomalies.
Both govern the update reaching the user with notice, A of the disruption it causes, B of its availability and delivery.
Both require managed handling of security-relevant assets across their lifecycle, A of security parameters, B of AI assets.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus the use of independent security testers.
Orderly network reconnection versus evaluation of access control frameworks.
